text.p: Earnings for Swedish metals and mining group Trelleborg AB for calendar year 1996.
- for A and B shares (crowns) 3.0 vs 3.0
- for C and D shares 10.0 vs 10.0
Other financial items CHARGE 14 vs 15 CHARGE
NOTE -- In a Reuters poll of eight analysts, expectations averaged a profit after financial items of 1.02 billion crowns.
"The listing in Toronto will be seen as an important industrial step in making Boliden an international company," Trelleborg's managing director Kjell Nilsson said in a statement.
"Toronto is the mining world's financial centre and the base for a large number of international mining house."
He said the capital gain through listing and selling off part of Boliden would be used for the expansion plans and to expand Trelleborg in other areas.
Boliden's managing director Anders Bulow said there were a number of possibilities.
"We have today a number of interesting suggestions for expansion on the mining side, both concerning prospects and mining projects," Bulow said in the statement.
He said the sale of Trelleborg's shares in Boliden would happen firstly to investors in and outside Canada, but with preference given to Trelleborg's current shareholders.
"Trelleborg will remain the largest owner of Boliden," the company said.
Trelleborg on Wednesday announced a fall in 1996 profits.
The company posted a profit after financial items excluding restructing costs of 1.02 billion crowns compared to 1.55 billion crowns in 1995.
Sales for the year fell to 20.57 billion crowns from 21.30 billion.
Trelleborg proposed an unchanged dividend of three crowns for A and B-series shares and of 10 crowns for C and D series shares.
